judged_text: deleteEvent uses the same dead fallback — find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId) when externalCalendarId is already falsy — so calendarId is always undefined for references without an externalCalendarId. Canceling such a booking throws inside calendar.events.delete (caught and logged), and the event stays on the host's Google calendar after cancellation, complete with its conferencing link, while Cal.com frees the slot — ghost events for attendees and double-booked time for the host.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` were changed to derive a calendar id via `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (because the ternary uses the `: ...find(...)` branch). When `externalCalendarId` is `undefined`/`null`, this `find` predicate is effectively `cal.externalId === undefined|null`, so it will almost always return `undefined`, yielding an undefined calendar id instead of falling back to the main/primary destination calendar as the old code did (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`). This is a concrete correctness regression in the diff, consistent with deletions/updates not targeting the intended calendar when a reference lacks `externalCalendarId`.
